question: How to attend Art Basel Paris
reponse_courte: Public and Premium tickets for the October 21 to 25, 2026 edition at the Grand Palais are on sale at artbasel.com: public days run from October 23 to 25, with the VIP preview on October 21 and 22 by invitation card from the galleries or from Art Basel's VIP Relations program. Journalists who can show a media affiliation go through the press accreditation portal.
details:
Art Basel Paris takes place at the Grand Palais from October 21 to 25, 2026: VIP preview on October 21 and 22, public days from October 23 to 25. Public tickets and Premium tickets, which open the doors to the October 22 vernissage, are on sale at artbasel.com. The free route runs through the galleries: a VIP preview card can be obtained from a participating gallery where you are a client, or a serious prospect; Art Basel also issues its own cards through its VIP Relations program. Journalists with a media affiliation access the VIP days through press accreditation, via Art Basel's portal.

The week also offers free doors in the fair's orbit, at the auction houses. Sotheby's Paris (76 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré) opens freely the exhibition preceding its "Modernités" evening sale, scheduled for Friday, October 23, 2026 at 5 pm to capture the major collectors passing through town; to bid, you must register on sothebys.com. Artcurial, in the Marcel Dassault private mansion (7 Rond-Point des Champs-Élysées), offers a free public opening and exhibition around its "La Modernité en partage" sale on Saturday, October 24, 2026; bidder registration is handled via artcurial.com.

question: How to get on board a yacht in Monaco
reponse_courte: The route open to everyone is the Monaco Yacht Show, September 23 to 26, 2026 at Port Hercule: passes are sold exclusively online, at €700 for a one-day pass from Thursday to Saturday, €1,300 for 2 days and €2,070 for 3 days. For a private evening aboard a superyacht, such as the My Yacht Group party during the show, access is by invitation with mandatory RSVP.
details:
The Monaco Yacht Show, organized by Informa Markets at Port Hercule from September 23 to 26, 2026, is the most direct door. Official prices, taxes included: €400 for Wednesday, September 23, a day reserved for invited guests and private clients with Dockside access; €700 per day from Thursday to Saturday; €1,300 for 2 days; €2,070 for 3 days. Sales are exclusively online, with no box office on site, and the most sought-after categories sell out before summer: best to buy your pass as soon as ticketing opens. An official VIP program and a Press Pass can be obtained on request from the organizer.

To step aboard in the evening, the reference is the My Yacht Group private party, held aboard a superyacht moored at Port Hercule during the show. It is invitation-only, with mandatory RSVP: the organizer publishes contact details for receiving requests, and you must introduce yourself (profile, company, reason for attending) then wait for the list to be confirmed. Write as soon as summer ends, because the list closes before the show opens and late requests are no longer processed. Evening dress or a long gown is required; the price is not published.

question: What to wear to the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe
reponse_courte: Strict dress, jacket and tie, is the code listed for the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, on October 3 and 4, 2026 at the ParisLongchamp racecourse. On its official ticketing site, France Galop recommends an elegant but relaxed outfit, notes that hats are always welcome, and advises against very high heels, which make walking around the racecourse difficult.
details:
Our event page lists strict dress, jacket and tie, for the October 3 and 4, 2026 edition at ParisLongchamp. On its official ticketing site, France Galop publishes its own advice, verified in August 2026: an elegant but relaxed outfit, hats always welcome, and reasonable heels, since very high heels make walking around the racecourse difficult.

As for access, everything is booked through the official France Galop ticketing site, with dynamic pricing: prices rise as the date approaches. In 2026, expect from €10 for the Village de l'Arc, from €20 for the general enclosure, from €60 for the Pelouse de l'Arrivée Or, from €80 for the Sommet de l'Arc, from €110 for the Bistro Triomphe Hespéride and from €300 for the Tribune de l'Arrivée Or. Hospitality packages range from €239 (Brasserie ParisLongchamp) to €827 (Prestige Cascade), including the Ribot package at €659. Book early: the Prestige Cascade hospitality and the Tribune de l'Arrivée Or, the best-placed options, are the first to sell out.

question: What is the black tie dress code
reponse_courte: Black tie is the evening code of the dinner jacket: a black wool dinner jacket, single-breasted, without vents, with silk peak lapels or a shawl collar, worn with a bow tie you tie yourself, according to Debrett's. It is the code of the great galas, such as the amfAR Gala in Cannes.
details:
The rule comes from Debrett's, whose guide "Deconstructing Dress Codes" was verified in August 2026. A black tie dinner jacket is recognized by four details: black wool, single-breasted, no vents, silk peak lapels or a shawl collar. The bow tie is tied by hand, never pre-tied. Not to be confused with white tie, an even more formal code, which requires a black tailcoat with silk lapels worn open over a shirt fastened with removable dress studs.

On the ground, black tie is the code of the great galas. The amfAR Gala in Cannes presents itself this way in the foundation's press releases: a black tie event moving from cocktails to dinner, then a live auction led by Simon de Pury. In the same register, the Monaco Red Cross Gala requires formal gala dress: donors are expected from 7:45 pm in the Salle des Etoiles, dinner is served at 8:30 pm and admission is reserved for guests aged 7 and over. One last point of protocol, valid for all these evenings: every invitation calls for a prompt reply, acceptance or refusal, and going back on your word at the last minute is considered rude.

question: How much does a ticket to the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe cost
reponse_courte: From €10 in the Village de l'Arc and €20 for the general enclosure, on the official France Galop ticketing site. The other enclosure categories range from €60 (Pelouse de l'Arrivée Or) to €300 (Tribune de l'Arrivée Or), and hospitality packages from €239 to €827. Pricing is dynamic: prices climb as October 3 and 4, 2026 approach.
details:
The Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe is run on October 3 and 4, 2026 at the ParisLongchamp racecourse, and everything is booked through the official France Galop ticketing site. Pricing is dynamic: the amounts announced are starting prices, which climb as the date approaches. Inside the racecourse, expect from €10 in the Village de l'Arc, from €20 for the general enclosure, from €60 in the Pelouse de l'Arrivée Or, from €80 at the Sommet de l'Arc, from €110 at the Bistro Triomphe Hespéride and from €300 in the Tribune de l'Arrivée Or.

Hospitality packages, with lunch and a view of the finish line, run as follows: Brasserie ParisLongchamp €239, Prestige €299, Prestige Brasserie €467, Prestige Auberge €599, the Ribot package €659 and Prestige Cascade €827. Third-party providers approved by France Galop also offer them, including Racing Breaks for the British market. The trap is the calendar: the Prestige Cascade hospitality and the Tribune de l'Arrivée Or, the best-placed options, are the first to sell out. Booking early therefore means both securing a seat and paying less. One last detail noted on our event page: strict dress, jacket and tie, is required.

question: How to get a box at the Wiener Philharmoniker Ball
reponse_courte: By writing directly to the Wiener Philharmoniker: box orders are placed exclusively in writing, by post or email, in the August preceding the ball, with every request placed on a waiting list and allocated according to availability. For the edition of Thursday, January 21, 2027, expect from €6,000 (Belvédère box) to €18,000 (a 10-person parterre box).
details: The Wiener Philharmoniker sell their boxes directly, through their Kartenbüro and ball office at Kärntner Ring 12, 1010 Vienna. Orders must be sent in writing in the August preceding the ball, so the timeline is tight; allocation follows availability and every request goes onto a waiting list. Official prices for the January 21, 2027 edition: parterre box €18,000 for 10 people or €15,600 for 8, standing parterre box €8,000 for 8, premium balcony box €14,520 for 12, balcony box €8,000 for 8, Belvédère box €6,000 for 6. Failing a box, table seats (€105 to €180) are already sold out for 2027; what remains are individual entrance cards at €220, on sale from January 11, 2027 at the Kärntner Ring 12 box office and online. No free invitation exists. The only reduced-price route is the opening committee, by registration with the Tanzschule Elmayer from September onward, couples only, with a mandatory audition in the autumn (card at €65): a minimum age of 17 for young women and 18 for young men, the left-turning waltz required, married couples not admitted, and mandatory rehearsals at the Musikverein the week before the ball. On the night, doors open at 9 pm, the ball begins at 10 pm and ends at 5 am; a full-length evening gown and a tailcoat are required.

question: What to wear to a gala
reponse_courte: As a general rule, a gala is held in black tie: a dinner jacket for men, an evening gown, preferably full length, for women. The invitation is the authority: it states the dress code, and the dress code rules.
details: The benchmark is black tie, the code of nearly all major evening galas. According to Debrett's, it requires men to wear a black wool dinner jacket, single-breasted, without vents, with silk peak lapels or a shawl collar, and a bow tie tied by hand. For women, the evening gown, preferably full length, is the safe choice. On the calendar, the amfAR Gala in Venice (Sunday, September 6, 2026, Molino Stucky) is billed as black tie, as are the opening galas of the Metropolitan Opera and the New York Philharmonic; amfAR's press releases also present its Cannes gala as a black tie event, with cocktails, dinner and then an auction. Some galas set out their own protocol: at the Monaco Red Cross Gala, formal gala dress is required, donors are expected from 7:45 pm in the Salle des Étoiles and dinner is served at 8:30 pm. Two rules complete the outfit. First, the invitation is the authority: it states the code, and any doubt is settled with the organizer, never by improvising. Second, every invitation calls for a prompt reply, acceptance or refusal, and you do not cancel at the last minute. Finally, do not confuse black tie with white tie: the tailcoat, reserved for the most ceremonial evenings such as the great Viennese balls, is another register altogether.

question: How to attend Royal Ascot
reponse_courte: Tickets are sold on Ascot's official ticketing site, eticketing.co.uk/ascotracecourse, from £25 in the Windsor Enclosure. The 2027 edition runs from Tuesday, June 15 to Saturday, June 19; only the Royal Enclosure is not for sale, it is obtained through sponsorship by two members.
details: Tickets are booked on Ascot's official ticketing site, eticketing.co.uk/ascotracecourse (Ticketmaster Sport UK, with a virtual queue). The 2027 edition runs from Tuesday, June 15 to Saturday, June 19. Three enclosures sell freely: the Windsor Enclosure from £25, with no formal dress code and picnics allowed; the Queen Anne Enclosure from £80, with a dress code enforced; and the Village Enclosure, the festival enclosure with an after-party, 2027 prices to come. The Royal Enclosure, however, cannot be bought: you must be sponsored by two members who have belonged for at least 5 years and count at least 4 years of actual attendance, and who know the candidate personally. The application is signed by both sponsors, carries a £100 fee, takes up to 3 weeks to process and must be filed before mid-May; badges can be reserved from January 2027. An alternative without sponsorship: booking a table at one of the Royal Enclosure restaurants (Panoramic, Parade Ring). Hospitality packages from the official supplier (eventmasters.co.uk) range from around £252 per person at the Terrace Club to more than £2,940. Mind the dress code, strict in the Royal Enclosure and Queen Anne (details at ascot.com/royal-ascot/handbook). No free route exists, apart from professional press accreditation via the portal accreditation.ascot.com.

question: What is a guest list
reponse_courte: A guest list is the named list of invitees settled by the organizer before an event: only the names on it get through the door. It cannot be bought: you are added by invitation, or after a request approved by the organizer.
details: A guest list is drawn up by the organizer, its press office or its client relations team, and settled before the event: at the door, a name is checked, not a ticket. In the world this site covers, it has two constant features. First, it is name-based: at Paris Fashion Week (Spring-Summer 2027 ready-to-wear, from September 28 to October 6, 2026), each house invites by name through its press office and client relations team, and FHCM accreditation, necessary for the press, is not sufficient: each house decides its own guests. Second, it closes: for the MY Yacht Monaco party, aboard a superyacht in Port Hercule during the Monaco Yacht Show (September 23 to 26, 2026), the list closes before the show opens and late requests are no longer processed; you must introduce yourself (profile, company, reason for attending) and wait for the organizer's approval. How to get on it: either you are invited (accredited press, buyer, client, friend of the house), or you ask to be, by writing to the organizer early with a serious reason. What does not work: showing up at the door without being on the list, or trying to buy your place. The houses' rule admits no exception: no place can be bought, it is earned through the relationship.

question: What is a dress code
reponse_courte: A dress code is the standard of dress set by the host or organizer of an event, stated on the invitation or the ticket. It is not a suggestion: in the strictest enclosures, a non-compliant outfit means refused entry, with no ticket refund.
details: A dress code lets the host guarantee the unity of the evening, and lets the visitor know exactly what is expected before walking through the door. On the invitations recorded by this site, it runs from the most relaxed to the strictest: smart casual with a hat recommended at the polo, all-white dress required at the summer white parties, strict jacket and tie at the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, on October 3 and 4, 2026 at ParisLongchamp, evening dress and black tie for galas, up to the tailcoat of the great Viennese balls. Three things to know. First, it is applied to the letter: La Scala refuses spectators in shorts or tank tops entry to the auditorium, without refunding the ticket, and the Stewards' Enclosure at Henley refuses entry to women whose hemline does not fall below the knee. Second, it can be measured in numbers: in the Royal Enclosure at Royal Ascot, hats are compulsory for women and a headpiece is accepted only if its base is at least 10 cm in diameter. Finally, it varies by enclosure within a single event: at Royal Ascot 2027, from June 15 to 19, the Windsor Enclosure (from £25) imposes no formal dress code, while the Queen Anne and the Royal Enclosure apply theirs strictly.

question: What is a hospitality package at an event
reponse_courte: A hospitality package is a paid formula that adds to the entry ticket a reserved space, catering and a prime position. It is the official route to comfort at the great fixtures, sold by the organizer or by its approved providers.
details: The clearest example is the Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, on October 3 and 4, 2026 at ParisLongchamp. France Galop sells basic entry from €10 (Village de l'Arc), but offers above it a range of hospitality packages: Brasserie ParisLongchamp €239, Prestige €299, Prestige Brasserie €467, Prestige Auberge €599, the Ribot package €659, Prestige Cascade €827. Third-party providers approved by France Galop also distribute them, including Racing Breaks for the British market. Two traps: pricing is dynamic, with prices rising as the date approaches, and the best-placed offers (Prestige Cascade, Tribune de l'Arrivée Or) are the first to sell out. The same logic applies at Royal Ascot, June 15 to 19, 2027: packages from Ascot's official supplier (eventmasters.co.uk) range from around £252 per person (Terrace Club) to more than £2,940 (Panoramic, Parade Ring Restaurant). At the Monaco Grand Prix, announced for June 3 to 6, 2027 by the Automobile Club de Monaco (dates still subject to the FIA's validation of the F1 calendar in autumn 2026), the ACM offers its VIP Belvédère and Loges packages, lounge and catering included (hospitalite@acm.mc), while the F1 Paddock Club is distributed via formula1.com. In every case, hospitality is bought from the organizer or from its officially approved providers.

question: How to attend Paris Fashion Week
reponse_courte: Shows on the official calendar are not open to the public: each house invites by name, with the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode (FHCM) accrediting press and professional buyers. For the September 28 to October 6, 2026 edition, four routes exist: accredited press, registered buyers, VIC clients, and guests of the houses. No seat can be bought.
details:
The Spring-Summer 2027 ready-to-wear edition runs from September 28 to October 6, 2026, at venues across Paris, under the aegis of the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode (FHCM), which organizes the official calendar. Shows are by invitation from the houses, and each house alone decides who is invited. Four routes exist. The press: FHCM accreditation is free (accreditation@fhcm.paris), but it is necessary without being sufficient; you must then secure an invitation from the press office of the house in question. Registered professional buyers are the second route. The third is that of clients, known as VICs: a lasting client relationship with a house, a single sales advisor and a purchase history open the door to invitations and the front row. The fourth covers friends of the house and public figures.

The classic trap is believing that accreditation is enough, or that a seat can be paid for. No seat at a show can be bought: it is earned through the relationship. For anyone starting from zero, the realistic path therefore runs either through a press title and an accreditation request to the FHCM, or through loyalty in boutique with one specific house. The detailed show calendar is published by the FHCM.

question: How to get invited to a fashion show
reponse_courte: Two paths exist: free press accreditation from the FHCM (accreditation@fhcm.paris) followed by a request to the press office of the house in question, or VIC client status, built in boutique through a purchase history with a single sales advisor. No seat can be bought: an invitation is earned through the relationship.
details:
The press route begins with the FHCM's free accreditation (accreditation@fhcm.paris); you must then write to the press office of the house you are targeting to request an invitation to its show, for the week of September 28 to October 6, 2026. Each house (Dior, Chanel, Saint Laurent, Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Loewe, Givenchy) works through its own press office or a press relations agency; the leading Paris agencies are Karla Otto, KCD and Lucien Pagès Communication, along with the LVMH group's own press operation.

The route without a press card is that of the client. Become a client of a house, build loyalty with a single sales advisor in boutique, and express the wish to be invited: a significant purchase history qualifies you for VIC status, which opens invitations to the shows and the front row. The trap to avoid is believing that a seat can be sold: no invitation can be bought, and FHCM accreditation itself is necessary but not sufficient, since each house decides its own guests. The relationship, editorial or commercial, is the only currency that counts.

question: What to wear to the opera
reponse_courte: For an ordinary performance, no mandatory evening dress appears in any of the regulations we have checked: polished city attire is enough. The only written prohibition is La Scala's, which refuses entry to the auditorium in shorts or a tank top, without refunding the ticket.
details:
La Scala's audience information rules, checked in August 2026, are explicit: patrons in shorts or tank tops are not admitted to the auditorium, and the ticket is not refunded. It is the only written dress requirement our registry records for an ordinary performance.

At the Paris Opera, the rule verified in the house's attendance regulations concerns punctuality rather than wardrobe: the auditorium doors close as soon as the performance has begun, and latecomers can only be seated at intermission if the running of the show allows for it, with no exchange or refund of the ticket. Arriving early is therefore part of the outfit. The register changes for ball evenings held in opera houses: at the Vienna Opera Ball, the regulations require gentlemen to wear a black tailcoat with white shirt, white bow tie and black patent leather shoes, and ladies a floor-length ball gown. For an ordinary evening, settle on polished city attire, with no formal requirement on record beyond the minimum set by La Scala.

question: What is white tie?
reponse_courte: White tie is the most formal and the rarest evening dress code: it calls for a black tailcoat with silk lapels, worn open, over a white shirt fastened with removable studs, according to Debrett's. It is the dress of the great Viennese balls, completed by a white bow tie and black patent leather shoes, with a floor-length ball gown for ladies.
details:
Debrett's, whose rules were checked in August 2026, describes white tie as the most formal and rarest code: a black tailcoat with silk lapels, always worn open, and a white shirt fastened with removable studs, not sewn-on buttons. This is what sets it apart from black tie, which is built around the dinner jacket.

The Viennese balls apply it to the letter. At the Vienna Opera Ball, whose 69th edition takes place on Thursday, February 4, 2027, the official regulations require gentlemen to wear a black tailcoat with white shirt, white bow tie and black patent leather shoes, with gala uniform admitted as an option. Ladies wear a floor-length ball gown, in any color; traditional costume and the festive dirndl are expressly excluded. The same requirement applies at the Ball der Wiener Philharmoniker, on Thursday, January 21, 2027 at the Musikverein: long evening gown and tailcoat. Both evenings begin at 10 pm and end at 5 am.

question: How much does New Year's Eve at a palace hotel cost?
reponse_courte: The only rate published in our file is La Mamounia's: from 4,200 to 8,000 Moroccan dirhams (MAD) per person for the 2025 edition, depending on the dining room, with 2026 prices yet to be released. At the other palace hotels we track (Gstaad Palace, Badrutt's Palace, Eden Rock, Cheval Blanc St-Barth), the December 31 dinner is a paid event but its price is not published: it is available on request from the house.
details:
The only published benchmark is La Mamounia's: for the 2025 edition, New Year's Eve ranged from 4,200 to 8,000 Moroccan dirhams (MAD) per person depending on the dining room chosen; rates for December 31, 2026 are yet to be released. Everywhere else, the gala dinner is a paid event but its price is not posted: you ask for it directly.

At the Gstaad Palace, whose winter season opens on December 15, 2026, the December 31 gala dinner is booked through guestrelations@palace.ch, rate on request; for reference, the GreenGo after-party on January 1, 2026 was CHF 400 per person, with nothing yet published for 2027. At Badrutt's Palace, the season runs from December 3, 2026 to March 30, 2027; the New Year's Eve program and rates appear from autumn onward, and December 31 sells out very far in advance. On Saint-Barthélemy, neither Eden Rock, where tables go first to hotel guests, nor Cheval Blanc St-Barth, whose multi-course dinner is paired with grands crus, publishes its prices; for Cheval Blanc, the island's guides advise booking 3 to 4 months ahead. The rule of the genre never changes: book early and ask the house itself for the rate.

question: When to book the LVMH Journées Particulières
reponse_courte: Reservations open in the course of September 2026 on the official website lvmh.com, for the October 16 to 18, 2026 edition; no precise opening date has been published. Sign up now via the site's email alert form to be notified, and book your slot the moment reservations open.
details: The official website announces only that reservations will open at some point in September 2026, with no precise day, for the edition running from Friday, October 16 to Sunday, October 18, 2026. As of August 29, 2026, roughly 7 weeks before the event, ticketing by venue and time slot had not yet opened: none of the venue pages consulted showed a booking button, only practical information. In the meantime, the site offers an email alert sign-up form: this is the way to be notified when the "Carnet d'expériences" opens, and to book your slot right away. Booking is free, with no code or referral required, subject to available places, and each venue applies its own age and access conditions. As for the traps: there is no paid ticket, no VIP access for sale, and no official resale; any route other than lvmh.com should therefore be ruled out. On Place Vendôme, the "Diadèmes de Rêve" visit at Chaumet (12 Place Vendôme) and the opening of the Repossi boutique (6 Place Vendôme) follow the same calendar: registrations opening in the course of September 2026 via the Journées Particulières website, by selecting the desired experience as soon as it is published.

question: What do women wear for black tie?
reponse_courte: An evening gown, preferably long; a very dressy cocktail dress is accepted at most galas. Color is free, fabrics should remain refined, and when in doubt, the long gown is welcome everywhere.
details: Black tie sets a strict rule for men (Debrett's: black wool dinner jacket, single-breasted, no vents, peaked silk lapels or a shawl collar, self-tied bow tie) but leaves women real latitude. The safe choice is the long evening gown; a very dressy cocktail dress works at most galas, outside the most ceremonial evenings. Color is free, and black is by no means required; favor refined fabrics (silk, crêpe, velvet), pumps and a clutch, with a stole over the shoulders if needed. Two traps. The first is underestimating the venue: when the invitation specifies a long gown, the cocktail dress no longer passes. The great Viennese balls, more formal still than black tie since they require the tailcoat, put it in writing: at the Vienna Opera Ball (Thursday, February 4, 2027), a floor-length ball gown is mandatory, any color admitted, with traditional costume and dirndl expressly excluded; at the Ball der Wiener Philharmoniker (Thursday, January 21, 2027), a long evening gown is required. The second is the opposite misreading: black tie is not cocktail attire, and a short daytime dress has no place there. One example on the calendar: the amfAR gala in Venice, on Sunday, September 6, 2026 at the Molino Stucky, is black tie.

question: How does an auction work?
reponse_courte: The pre-sale exhibition is public and free; to bid, you simply register free of charge with the auction house, with ID and proof of address, and collect a numbered paddle. Bidding generally opens below the low estimate and rises in increments of up to 10 percent; once placed, a bid cannot be withdrawn.
details: Everything begins with the public pre-sale exhibition, free and open to all, where the lots can be examined up close (handling them, however, is at the visitor's own risk). To bid, you must register with the house: Christie's recommends doing so at least 24 hours before the sale, and the paddle is collected on presentation of photo ID and proof of address; at Phillips, absentee bids and telephone bid requests must also arrive at least 24 hours in advance. No paid ticket is required. In the saleroom, bidding generally opens below the low estimate and moves up in increments of up to 10 percent, at the auctioneer's discretion. A cardinal rule: a bid is irrevocable, and can no longer be canceled once placed. The winning lot is invoiced to the name and address under which the paddle was registered, with no transfer possible. For lots of very high value, a financial guarantee or deposit may be required per lot. Two dates illustrate the calendar: Sotheby's Paris evening sale Modernités, on Friday, October 23, 2026 at 5 pm (exhibition free to visit, registration on sothebys.com), and Christie's Magnificent Jewels sale in Geneva, on November 10, 2026, with registration via a My Christie's account.

question: What is the front row at a fashion show?
reponse_courte: The front row is the first row of seats at a fashion show, running along the runway, reserved for the house's most important guests: top-tier press, celebrities, major buyers and best clients. These seats cannot be bought: each house assigns them by name.
details: At fashion shows, guests are seated by row, and placement signals status: the front row, the first row facing the runway, goes to editors-in-chief, celebrities, major buyers and the house's best clients. Being seen there is as much part of the event as the collection itself. The front row is not for sale. At Paris Fashion Week (Spring-Summer 2027 ready-to-wear, September 28 to October 6, 2026), the official calendar shows are by personal invitation from the houses, and the site's access guides know only one route to the first row for anyone who is neither press nor a buyer: client status. Building a lasting client relationship with a house, with the same sales advisor and a significant purchase history, qualifies you for VIC status, which opens invitations to the shows and the front row. For the press, FHCM accreditation (free, via accreditation@fhcm.paris) grants access to the official calendar, but the invitation, and all the more so the row, remain at the discretion of each house's press office. The rule holds for the whole show, and first of all for its front row: no seat can be bought, it is earned through the relationship.

question: What is an auction paddle?
reponse_courte: The paddle is the numbered panel the auction house hands to each registered bidder: raised in the saleroom, it signals a bid to the auctioneer. It is obtained free of charge, upon prior registration with ID and proof of address.
details: The paddle is collected before the sale, on presentation of photo ID and proof of address; Christie's recommends registering at least 24 hours before the session. At Christie's, registration goes through a My Christie's account on christies.com or through the sale office, with a payment method on file: a paddle number is then issued. For the Magnificent Jewels sale on November 10, 2026 in Geneva, no paid ticket is required: this free registration alone opens the saleroom, though a financial guarantee or deposit may be required for lots of very high value, with amounts published alongside the catalogue. The same logic applies at Sotheby's: for the Modernités evening sale on October 23, 2026 in Paris, bidders register on sothebys.com. Three rules to know before raising your paddle. Any winning lot is invoiced to the name and address under which the paddle was registered, with no transfer to another name possible. Once placed, a bid can no longer be canceled. Finally, bidding generally opens below the low estimate and moves up in increments of up to 10 percent, at the auctioneer's discretion.

question: What is morning dress?
reponse_courte: Morning dress, la jaquette in French, is the most formal daytime ceremonial attire in the men's wardrobe: a long tailed coat worn with a waistcoat and top hat. It is the code required of gentlemen in the Royal Enclosure at Royal Ascot.
details: Morning dress is to the daytime what black tie and white tie are to the evening: the most formal degree. It is not to be confused with the black tie dinner jacket or the white tie tailcoat; it is their daytime equivalent, reserved for ceremonies and the races. Its most codified territory is the Royal Enclosure at Royal Ascot, June 15 to 19, 2027, where the formal dress code requires morning dress and a hat. The rules published by Ascot are precise: a black, grey or navy morning coat; a black or grey top hat is mandatory, and may only be removed in a restaurant, a private box, an enclosed outdoor seating area, a terrace, a balcony or a garden; any customization of the top hat (colored ribbons, feathers, ornaments) is prohibited. Ladies answer to the same degree of formality: a hat is mandatory, and a headpiece is only accepted if its base measures at least 10 cm in diameter. One last reminder: the Royal Enclosure cannot be bought. Entry comes through sponsorship by two members who have been affiliated for at least five years, a signed application and a £100 fee, with badges bookable from January 2027. Morning dress is the customary condition, not the pass.

question: What is a vernissage
reponse_courte: A vernissage is the opening night of an exhibition, held before the doors open to the general public, usually by invitation from the gallery, the fair or the auction house. The word comes from the day when painters would varnish their canvases before the Salons opened. It is the first access to the works, and the moment when the art world gathers.
details: The word comes from a custom of the painting Salons: the day before opening, artists would come to varnish their canvases in front of their close circle and their first buyers. What remains of it is the opening night, where the works are seen before anyone else and where the gallerist introduces artists to collectors. Today the term covers very different realities of access. The gallery vernissage remains the most open, usually by invitation from the gallery. The fair vernissage is the most tightly filtered in the market: at Frieze London, the first day, Wednesday 14 October 2026, is reserved for invited guests only, and Thursday from 11 am to 1 pm remains reserved for members and guests before general admission. Auction houses offer the most accessible version: the pre-sale exhibition. At Sotheby's Paris, 76 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, the exhibition preceding the Modernités evening sale on Friday 23 October 2026 at 5 pm is free to enter; only those who wish to bid must register on sothebys.com. The same spirit prevails at Christie's in Geneva: the public exhibition before the Magnificent Jewels sale on 10 November 2026 is traditionally free and open to all, with no invitation or registration. For anyone who wants to get close to the art world, the pre-sale vernissage is the simplest door: you see masterpieces without an invitation card, before they enter private collections.

question: What does VIC mean in fashion
reponse_courte: VIC stands for Very Important Client: the status a fashion house grants its most loyal clients. It is built through a significant purchase history with a single sales advisor, and it opens the door to show invitations and the front row.
details: The acronym comes from the English Very Important Client. In fashion houses, it designates the inner circle of clients whose purchase history and loyalty earn the house's special attentions, starting with invitations to its events. It is the route into the shows for those who are neither journalists nor professional buyers. The process costs nothing in itself: no seat at a show can be bought, it is the relationship that grants access. Each house manages its VIC circle through its client services, in liaison with its press office, and invites by name. The detailed calendar, show by show, is published in early September.

question: What is an enclosure at the races
reponse_courte: An enclosure is a reserved area of a British racecourse: each has its own ticket, its own services and its own dress code. The word describes both a perimeter and a rank, from the enclosure open to all to Ascot's Royal Enclosure, accessible through sponsorship.
details: Royal Ascot, from 15 to 19 June 2027, illustrates the system: four enclosures, four worlds. Without sponsorship, a table at a Royal Enclosure restaurant (Panoramic, Parade Ring) grants access. The principle extends beyond racing: in the Stewards' Enclosure at the Henley regatta, hemlines fall below the knee and you step outside the enclosure to take a phone call.

question: What is a quadrille at a ball
reponse_courte: The quadrille is a collective set dance, performed in square formation by groups of couples moving through a sequence of figures. At the great Viennese balls, it brings the whole room together at set times: at the Vienna Opera Ball, the midnight quadrille at 12, with further quadrilles at 2 am and 4 am.
details: Vienna keeps the liveliest form of the tradition. At the 69th Vienna Opera Ball (Wiener Opernball), on Thursday 4 February 2027, the evening follows a fixed order published by the Staatsoper: doors at 8:15 pm, opening at 10 pm, the midnight quadrille on the stroke of 12, then quadrilles at 2 am and 4 am, before the ball ends at 5 am. The midnight quadrille is the moment when the entire room comes down onto the dance floor: unlike the opening, reserved for the committee of selected young couples, it belongs to all the guests. Traditionally, the figures are called out loud as the dance unfolds, which lets novices follow along; no audition is required, unlike for the opening committee, which demands mastery of the left-turning waltz. It is danced in full evening dress, as the ball's dress code is strict: black tailcoat, white shirt, white bow tie and black patent shoes for gentlemen, with gala uniform admitted as an option; a floor-length ball gown for ladies, in any color, with traditional costume and festive dirndl expressly excluded.

question: What does RSVP mean
reponse_courte: RSVP abbreviates the French formula "Répondez s'il vous plaît," printed on invitations to request a reply, whether you accept or decline. The protocol is constant: every invitation calls for a prompt reply, and one does not go back on an acceptance at the last minute.
details: The abbreviation appears at the bottom of invitation cards, often followed by a deadline and a contact. It commits you to reply either way: you confirm your attendance or you decline, but you never leave a card unanswered. The rule is set down by Debrett's: every invitation calls for a prompt reply, acceptance or refusal, and going back on your word at the last minute is considered rude. In the world of private parties, the RSVP is no decorative courtesy: it conditions access. At the MY Yacht Monaco party, held aboard a superyacht in Port Hercule during the Monaco Yacht Show, from September 23 to 26, 2026, the invitation comes with a mandatory RSVP to the organizer: you introduce yourself (profile, company, reason for the request), then await validation of the list. That list closes before the show opens, and a late request is no longer processed. Replying early therefore pays twice over: you hold your standing, and you keep your place. Three usages to remember: you reply through the channel indicated on the card and no other; you reply for the people named on the invitation, without bringing anyone else; and an acceptance is a commitment, a last-minute no-show being the most frowned-upon offense.

question: What does tenue de soirée mean
reponse_courte: On an invitation card, "tenue de soirée" calls for the most formal register: an evening gown, often floor-length, for women, and a tuxedo for men. It is the French equivalent of black tie; when the host specifies "robe longue" (long gown), a short dress is no longer an option.
details: The mention appears in two forms on the invitations catalogued by the site. The first, "Black tie (tenue de soirée)," is the strict reading: under the Debrett's rule in the protocol register, black tie requires men to wear a black wool tuxedo, single-breasted, without vents, with peaked silk lapels or a shawl collar, and a bow tie you tie yourself. That is the code of the amfAR gala in Venice, on Sunday, September 6, 2026 at the Molino Stucky, during the Mostra. The second, "Tenue de soirée / robe longue," spells out the expectation for women: it is the code of the MY Yacht Monaco party, aboard a superyacht in Port Hercule during the Monaco Yacht Show (September 23 to 26, 2026), and of the summer parties of the palace hotels, from the Hôtel du Palais in Biarritz to the Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc. Above tenue de soirée there is only one degree: white tie, the tailcoat, reserved for the most formal balls and galas. Below come cocktail attire and business dress. The classic trap is confusing evening dress with dark dress: a business suit, even a black one, is not tenue de soirée as invitation cards mean it, and the tuxedo remains the right answer for men.

question: What is an evening sale
reponse_courte: The evening sale is an auction house's prestige session: it gathers the season's major lots before a room of registered bidders, on a date chosen for the presence of major collectors. The exhibition that precedes it, by contrast, remains free and open to all.
details: The Sotheby's Paris calendar provides the model. The "Modernités" evening sale takes place on Friday, October 23, 2026 at 5 pm, at 76 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, scheduled during Art Basel Paris week to capture the major collectors passing through: an evening sale always aligns with the moments when the art world is in town. Two phases, two publics. Before the sale, the public exhibition is free and open to all: anyone can come see the works, bearing in mind that handling an object on display in the house's premises is done at the visitor's own risk. Come evening, the room is reserved for registered bidders: for "Modernités," registration is on sothebys.com or through the Sotheby's Paris switchboard. The usages of the auction world fully apply: the houses ask you to register in advance (at least 24 hours before the sale at Christie's), bidding generally opens below the low estimate and advances in increments that can reach 10 percent at the auctioneer's discretion, a bid once placed is irrevocable, and the lot is invoiced in the name under which the paddle was registered.

question: How does a ball ticket lottery work
reponse_courte: Some great balls allocate their individual entry tickets by lottery: you register during a short window, then the draw decides who may buy a ticket. At the Vienna Opera Ball, the €435 tickets can only be obtained this way.
details: The textbook case is the Vienna Opera Ball (69. Wiener Opernball, Thursday, February 4, 2027). Sales fall exclusively to the Opernball-Büro of the Wiener Staatsoper, which states that no other point of sale exists. Individual entry tickets, at €435 (including a €35 solidarity contribution to "Österreich hilft Österreich"), a maximum of four per person and with no seat, are not sold first come, first served: they are allocated by lottery among those who registered. For 2027, the registration window ran from June 1 at 10 am to June 5, 2026 at 11:59 pm; it is closed. The trap is therefore the calendar: five days of registration, eight months before the ball. Those who miss the draw fall back on the other channels: table seats at €665 (the €435 entry ticket included, a maximum of six per person, sold first come, first served since June 24, 2026 at 10 am), boxes, sold only directly by the ball office, from €15,000 to €27,000 depending on location, or simple spectator tickets, from €110 to €290. One non-commercial route remains: applying to the opening committee, free to enter on opernball.at, open until September 16, 2026, with a participation fee of €140 per person if admitted.
